subject.title: RFC 0024: Localization Runtime and Product Coverage

question: Should OpenClaw sponsor RFC 0024's shared product-wide localization contract, including Gateway localization metadata, recipient locale ownership, localized plugin metadata, and release coverage gates?
rationale: The proposal is internally coherent, but acceptance commits several independent product and compatibility owners to new long-lived contracts that cannot be inferred from existing localized surfaces.

options.title: Keep draft for owner review
options.body: Collect explicit Gateway, channels, UI/CLI, plugin, and release decisions in the required discussion thread before accepting the five-phase RFC.

options.title: Narrow to localization core
options.body: Accept only locale resolution, message descriptors, and compatibility-preserving adapters now, leaving metadata, recipient storage, and release gates for later RFCs.

options.title: Decline shared runtime scope
options.body: Continue surface-owned localization without adopting a product-wide runtime and coverage contract.

recommendation.title: Keep draft for owner review
recommendation.body: Collect explicit Gateway, channels, UI/CLI, plugin, and release decisions in the required discussion thread before accepting the five-phase RFC.

likelyOwner.reason: They supplied the most relevant prior localization direction and have adjacent Gateway/plugin contract history needed to coordinate the decision.
